scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The ballet-féerie originates in Russia as a synthesis of the French féerie theatrical genre and the Italian ballo grande dance style.
It evolves from a long history of European spectacle, including the Renaissance ballet de cour and 17th-century pièces à machines, which rely on the engineering of architects like Nicola Sabbatini.
In the 19th century, these influences merge with the Russian interest in narrative ballet, creating a genre that prioritizes visual transformation and ensemble performance.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The ballet-féerie serves as a popular, often commercialized form of entertainment that aims to provide a dreamlike experience for the audience.
It functions as a morality play, depicting the triumph of good over evil through the use of magic talismans and supernatural intervention.
Today it is a historical tradition.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky is the most significant figure associated with the genre, having composed The Sleeping Beauty and The Nutcracker within this framework.

The genre originates in France as a theatrical fairy play, or féerie, before being adapted into the Russian ballet-féerie. Other variants include the English fairy extravaganza and the Spanish comedia de magia.
The genre descends from the French féerie and the Italian ballo grande, serving as a precursor to modern spectacular stage productions.

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Ballet-féerie is parent of féerie, the French theatrical genre that provides the name and narrative structure.
Ballet-féerie is an influence of ballo grande, the Italian style that provides the dance characteristics.

rules: Original composition only — no sampling, no melody of any existing recording, no lyrics from any song.
